title: Fatimah al-Zahra
hook: his youngest daughter, of whom he said, Fatimah is a part of me (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Maria and the eclipse, and a father who wept and still told the truth about the sky. Your line was the eyes weep, the heart grieves. Did you name something sad plainly? Day eight hundred eighteen.

A young woman crosses a room in Medina, and another woman watching her notices something. She walks exactly like her father. Same pace, same way of carrying herself. The watcher is Aisha, and she tells this herself in Sahih al-Bukhari. The father is the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and he is ill. The daughter is Fatimah. He calls out to her, welcome, my daughter, and sits her beside him. Then he leans close and whispers something, and she starts to cry. He whispers again, and she laughs. Aisha asks what he said. Fatimah won't tell her. Today: Fatimah, and the title she carries.
screen: `SHE WALKS EXACTLY LIKE HER FATHER.` → `A WHISPER: SHE WEEPS.` → `ANOTHER: SHE LAUGHS.`

segments.voice: Fatimah kept the secret while her father lived. After he died, Aisha asked again, and this time she told, and the reports in Bukhari give her answer. The first whisper: he would not recover from this illness. So she wept. The second, in one telling: she would be the first of his family to follow him; in another, she would be a leader among the women of paradise. So she laughed. Look at what that means. The news that comforted her was that she would not be apart from him for long. That closeness runs through every report about them. In the Sunan of Abu Dawud, Aisha says that when Fatimah came in, he would stand up for her, kiss her, and seat her in his own place; and when he came to her, she did the same for him. A father standing up for his daughter. And in Bukhari he says it outright: Fatimah is a part of me, and whoever angers her angers me. Now the title. Muslims call her Fatimah al-Zahra. In Arabic, al-Zahra means the radiant one, the shining one. The reports we just heard don't use it; it's a name later generations gave her, and they explain it in different ways. Sunni and Shi'a Muslims both use it and both honor her deeply. In Shi'a devotion her name is spoken in prayers and gatherings, and given to daughters. Across all of them, one picture holds: a daughter who walked like her father, sat in his seat, and was called a part of him.
screen: `FIRST WHISPER: HE WOULD NOT RECOVER.` · `SECOND: SHE WOULD FOLLOW HIM SOON.` · `HE STOOD UP FOR HER.` · `AL-ZAHRA: THE RADIANT ONE.` · then, large: `FATIMAH IS A PART OF ME.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: honor a daughter. Sit, and breathe. Bring to mind a daughter: yours, a niece, a student, a friend's girl, or yourself as someone's daughter. See her coming into the room. In your mind, stand up for her, the way he stood for Fatimah, and give her your seat. What would you want her to hear from you? Hold one sentence of honor for her, plain and true. If you pray, you can make a quiet du'a for her. If not, just keep her in mind with care. The bell holds the time.
Al-Zahra. The radiant one: the title Muslims give Fatimah, the Prophet's daughter, whom he called a part of him. Today's word.
Your line: a part of him. Today, tell a daughter in your life, or a parent if you're the daughter, one specific thing you honor in her. Day eight hundred eighteen.

howItsDone: Muslims speak of Fatimah with deep honor, often adding a blessing after her name; Shi'a Muslims in particular remember her in prayers and gatherings, and Muslim families name daughters after her.

original.note: Arabic: the radiant, shining one; a title of Fatimah, daughter of the Prophet.

trapdoor: what you thought: al-Zahra is part of Fatimah's name.
what it means: a title, the radiant one, given to the daughter he called a part of him.
what a scholar hears: the whispered secret is in Bukhari through Aisha, the standing to greet her is in Abu Dawud, and the title al-Zahra comes later, with more than one explanation.

notes: Bukhari 3623–3626 numbering: the reports vary on the second whisper (leader of the women of paradise / of the believers; first of his family to follow him). The script combines them; confirm.
Abu Dawud 5217 numbering and paraphrase: confirm.
'In a world where that was not the custom' (standing for a daughter): soft historical claim with no text cited; cut if a Keeper prefers.
al-Zahra glossed as 'the radiant one'; the claim that the title is later and explained variously: confirm.
Index hook calls her his youngest daughter; the script leaves 'youngest' out under the claims rule.
Day 778 already used 'Fatimah is a part of me' briefly; this day leads with the deathbed whispers instead.
Editor: removed 'older woman' (an age claim, likely wrong for Aisha) and the uncited 'not the custom' line; dropped 'many' and 'often' from claims about Shi'a devotion and naming.

Audit: the teach had merged the two Bukhari versions into one second whisper; it now says plainly that the tellings differ (one: first of his family to follow him; another: leader of the women of paradise, with the 'first to follow' news in the first whisper).
